contracts.promise: Managed volume artifacts remain independent and overlapping layouts are refused before provisioning.
supported_paths: Dotted mount names retain distinct artifacts and independent stored data across remounts.
refused_paths: Overlapping managed mount or generated image/metadata/temporary/restore paths fail admission.
boundaries: The agent refuses invalid layouts before creating any workload volume directory.
Actual loop-backed ext4 remount persistence requires the provisioned Linux root gate; portable checks cannot substitute for it.

contracts.promise: Artifact signing credentials remain useful beyond the ordinary short-lived TLS leaf window.
supported_paths: A valid cluster artifact signature verifies two hours after signing.
refused_paths: A code-signing leaf cannot outlive its issuing CA.
boundaries: Cached signers are replaced before expiry and after expiry; verification still uses current cryptographic validity.

contracts.promise: Batch admission validates all workloads and caller authority before registration or dispatch.
supported_paths: Scoped authorized jobs and approved host execution can run.
refused_paths: Any out-of-scope, invalid or unowned test job refuses the entire batch.
boundaries: Follower forwarding preserves caller credentials; authenticated internal dispatch still validates intrinsic specs and test leases.

contracts.promise: Repository-scoped publication requires destination authority for every referenced descriptor.
supported_paths: Completed upload evidence survives restart for its exact repository generation, and legitimate destination references can be reused.
refused_paths: Global blob presence, failed completion and receipt-write failure cannot grant destination authority.
boundaries: Config, layer and child-index references and GET/HEAD probes are covered.
Collection, corruption and exact-generation retirement remove or preserve evidence according to ownership.

contracts.promise: Failed or canceled log flushes remain queryable and retryable, and final file capture rescans after EOF.
supported_paths: Direct and shared flushes preserve captured rows through data or checkpoint persistence failure and retry.
refused_paths: Unconfirmed persistence cannot discard rows or acknowledge a flush.
boundaries: Fresh and resumed file readers discover bytes written between EOF observation and child exit.

contracts.promise: Remote metrics archives preserve immutable node-owned history.
supported_paths: Generic queries see multiple owners; node APIs restrict reads to their owner.
refused_paths: Remote create collisions and invalid or unpersistable owner identity refuse instead of replacing history.
boundaries: Certificate root plus NodeId remains stable through leaf renewal; plaintext owners survive restarts and label changes.

contracts.promise: Dependent app revisions remain uncommitted until their same-apply migration has positively exited zero.
supported_paths: A successful acknowledged prerequisite permits the new app revision.
refused_paths: Failure, invalid prerequisite identity or unknown execution cannot commit a dependent revision.
boundaries: Blocked and failed migrations; follower forwarding; leadership handover; claimed app/job ownership.

contracts.promise: Repeated batch submissions retain independent execution ownership, terminal evidence and logical authorization scope.
supported_paths: Each committed equal-label execution has a separate canonical identity; acknowledged same-owner retries preserve its attempt.
Owned Process/Apple/Runc terminal and retirement provenance remain distinct; batch and coordinator restarts retain identity.
SSE and WebSocket follow selectors choose the committed remote execution owner with original logical authorization.
refused_paths: Missing mandatory ownership fields, wrong worker/spec/namespace/generation and stale callbacks cannot relabel or complete an execution.
Ordinary apply/internal dispatch cannot overwrite a retained execution identity; predictable whole-group refusal leaves no admission or partial startup.
Stalled local metadata returns bounded unavailability before launch, desired writes or owner mutation.
boundaries: Preparing/start/exit/retirement checkpoints and retained worker reports.
Same-label overlapping batches, leader/runner replacement, actual ProcessGrill lifecycle and controlled remote follow transports.
Required state-generation schema; absence/null are separately refused or accepted according to mandatory explicit ownership fields.

contracts.promise: Ingress route refresh preserves endpoint health and rejects stale probe results.
supported_paths: Failed endpoints recover after successful probes.
refused_paths: Repeated failed endpoints remain excluded after route replacement.
boundaries: An old-address probe cannot change the replacement address health.

contracts.promise: Ingress returns upstream redirects directly to the caller.
supported_paths: Both pooled and fresh clients preserve redirect status, location, cookies and body for supported redirect codes.
refused_paths: The proxy does not request the redirect destination on behalf of the caller.
boundaries: POST redirects, relative and absolute locations, and both upstream client paths are covered.

contracts.promise: The complete service catalogue preserves workloads beyond the bounded kernel backend pool.
supported_paths: Local and remote services with33 backends retain catalogue, DNS, ingress and cleanup ownership.
refused_paths: Failed endpoints cannot enter the selected dataplane pool.
boundaries: Consumer-specific bounded pools remain stable under catalogue reorder and favor healthy local endpoints.
Pure map conversion tests compile only on Linux; no live kernel steering proof is claimed by this provisional inventory.

contracts.promise: Registry token verification uses the shared API token check.
supported_paths: Bearer and Basic credentials on registry reads and writes authenticate through the shared API token check.
refused_paths: Malformed credentials return unauthorized before any hashing.
boundaries: Registry credentials go through the API token check, which hashes once with SHA-256 and runs inline since #912, so there is no admission permit to wait for.
Related TLS lifecycle fixtures check pooled connection retirement at the credential deadline, with a disabled-retirement negative control.

contracts.promise: All local blob writers reserve shared physical payload capacity before writing.
supported_paths: Registry, peer and runtime writes share a compressed CAS, temporary upload and repository receipt payload budget.
refused_paths: Bare blob accumulation, oversized chunks, repeated repository receipts and excess payload-file counts are refused before the refused write grows storage.
boundaries: Deduplication and upload-to-CAS moves transfer reservations without double charging.
Startup reconstructs committed, temporary, receipt and interrupted atomic-write payloads.
Failed cleanup retains charges; confirmed cancellation, collection and exact receipt retirement restore capacity.
The existing upload-cleanup fixture now distinguishes server-owned IO500 from malformed-session400 while preserving fencing and recovery.

contracts.promise: Cron parsing refuses invalid schedules and stepped evaluation terminates without integer wraparound.
supported_paths: A minute step of 255 selects only its mathematically valid minute.
refused_paths: Invalid schedule fields and zero steps fail configuration validation.
boundaries: All 60 minute values are checked for large single-value, bounded-range and wildcard steps.

contracts.promise: A batch refuses duplicate job names before registration or dispatch.
supported_paths: Each admitted batch job identity is unique.
refused_paths: Same-name submissions are refused even when their namespaces differ.
boundaries: Public submission and authenticated internal dispatch both refuse before queueing work; refused public batches have no registered status.

contracts.promise: Durably queued batches share live worker resource admission with apps; owned resources remain reserved until positive retirement.
supported_paths: Admission can queue runs without global capacity reports; execution requires current worker evidence and shared CPU/memory/FIFO permits.
Concurrent submissions deduplicate immutable runs and retained worker outcomes survive coordinator changes.
refused_paths: Stale or foreign grants and legacy callbacks cannot fabricate accepted completion.
Unknown retirement, abandoned attempts and cancelled waiters cannot release another live owner or invent resources.
boundaries: Common public admission versus worker dispatch; shared resource dimensions and FIFO; durable conservative restart fencing.

contracts.promise: Ingress keeps active responses alive while bounding inactive upstream waits.
supported_paths: Fresh and pooled clients complete an active response lasting beyond thirty seconds.
refused_paths: Stalled response headers and stalled body reads remain bounded.
boundaries: Both upstream client paths are covered.
Related capture repairs await reader publication or termination, preserve owned capture across waiter cancellation, and bound descendant-held pipes after child exit.

contracts.promise: External DNS uses the configured resolver over TCP, including retry after a truncated UDP response.
supported_paths: A direct external TCP query relays framed DNS bytes to the real loopback TCP upstream.
A truncated UDP answer preserves TC; an explicitly sent downstream TCP retry succeeds.
Internal TCP names are answered locally without forwarding.
refused_paths: An unavailable/stalled external TCP upstream returns SERVFAIL within the configured forward deadline.
Upstream frames with a wrong transaction ID or question are ignored before accepting the matching response.
boundaries: Both downstream TCP frame and upstream frame are exercised through actual sockets.
The test intentionally configures a loopback upstream and explicitly issues the TCP retry; it does not prove public DNS availability or an operating-system resolver automatic fallback.

contracts.promise: Refuse cross-namespace workload names that cannot be represented by bare-name configuration keys.
supported_paths: App, job and build trees retain each admitted workload.
refused_paths: Explicit or directory-derived namespaces containing the same workload name refuse compilation.
boundaries: No partial configuration may overwrite one namespace with another.

contracts.promise: Typed defaults merge inherited fields without overwriting explicit workload settings.
supported_paths: Resources, environment, nested deployment fields and explicit host execution inherit supported defaults.
refused_paths: Unknown default keys and invalid typed values return errors containing the default file path.
boundaries: Explicit scalar values, zero and false override inherited values; partial child tables preserve unspecified parent fields.

contracts.promise: CLI and GitOps resolve the same complete configuration tree.
supported_paths: Signed and unsigned watched subtrees inherit defaults and directory-derived namespaces.
refused_paths: Partial invalid trees, duplicate GitOps resources and cross-namespace name collisions refuse.
boundaries: The watched tree root remains independent from its directory-derived child namespace.

contracts.promise: GitOps refuses unsupported jobs before publishing any dependent declarative resources.
supported_paths: Apps, namespaces and permissions continue to synchronize.
refused_paths: Standalone, scheduled and migration-prerequisite jobs explicitly refuse.
boundaries: Refusal preserves the last applied revision and every desired resource.

contracts.promise: Dry-run comparison uses complete namespace-specific resource specifications and honest evidence availability.
supported_paths: Complete app, job, namespace and permission specifications can prove unchanged or changed resources.
refused_paths: Unavailable agent evidence, failed live comparison and another namespace's workload cannot prove an unchanged desired resource.
boundaries: Implicit default namespace and placement ordinals do not change desired fingerprints.
Same-image changes to workload settings change the fingerprint.
Offline or partial comparison is explicit in both text and JSON.

contracts.promise: Live admission validates namespace references against authoritative committed state.
supported_paths: Apps, builds and permissions may reference existing namespaces omitted from a partial manifest.
refused_paths: Missing namespaces and invalid intrinsic fields refuse before any write.
boundaries: Followers defer namespace existence to the authoritative leader.

contracts.promise: Configuration compilation refuses invalid input without emitting a partial result.
supported_paths: The CLI processes a directory tree only when its inputs can be read and parsed.
refused_paths: Malformed defaults, malformed workloads, invalid nested inputs and unreadable symlink inputs refuse the entire compile.
boundaries: An actual CLI process emits no partial stdout on refused input.

contracts.promise: A202 webhook acknowledgment represents retained coordinator admission rather than a discarded follower-local nudge.
supported_paths: Signed follower delivery reaches the leader and retained pending generation survives handover/restart.
refused_paths: Unavailable coordinator refuses retryably without consuming replay/rate reservations.
boundaries: Replicated trigger admission before202; stale completion cannot consume a newer generation; replay/rate rollback; bounded receipts.
Handover cases cover pending-trigger/replay retention before execution starts; complete Git sync has no captured leadership-term or atomic transaction fence.

contracts.promise: Autoscaling refuses invalid targets and cannot scale from nonfinite observations.
supported_paths: Finite targets above one requested resource unit are supported.
refused_paths: Nonpositive and nonfinite targets fail both configuration admission and autoscaler conversion.
boundaries: NaN and positive or negative infinity observations produce no scaling decision.

contracts.promise: Preserve owned mayo publication/retry state across the finite reviewed lifecycle controls.
supported_paths: Owned pending state remains visible and immutable retry/publication identity survives cancellation, collision and confirmed local writes.
refused_paths: Unconfirmed owned directory entries or foreign publications cannot produce a successful durability/visibility acknowledgement.
boundaries: Actual MayoStore and object_store interface using InMemory/controlled fault wrapper; no cloud network transport.

contracts.promise: Preserve owned ketchup publication/retry state across the finite reviewed lifecycle controls.
supported_paths: Owned pending state remains visible and immutable retry/publication identity survives cancellation, collision and confirmed local writes.
refused_paths: Unconfirmed owned directory entries or foreign publications cannot produce a successful durability/visibility acknowledgement.
boundaries: Actual LogStore local Parquet/JSON read/write/query with injected filesystem failure/publication gate.
Direct typed production/config/state function or local filesystem fixture; no external transport inferred.

contracts.promise: Preserve owned registry publication/retry state across the finite reviewed lifecycle controls.
supported_paths: Owned pending state remains visible and immutable retry/publication identity survives cancellation, collision and confirmed local writes.
refused_paths: Unconfirmed owned directory entries or foreign publications cannot produce a successful durability/visibility acknowledgement.
boundaries: Actual ImagePuller with controlled loopback registry and shared local BlobStore; not public-registry availability.
Actual public BlobStore operations and local filesystem/quota/receipt behavior; deterministic faults are not power cuts.

contracts.promise: A supported resourceful ordinary Runc job retains its exact committed capacity until the real terminal receipt settles, then a full-worker batch can actually complete.
supported_paths: Real HTTP ordinary apply, Council claim and owned Runc child; valid nonzero request=limit CPU/memory.
Exact terminal receipt watcher settles the original claim after the real child exits zero, allowing actual batch placement and child completion.
refused_paths: Full-worker, CPU-only saturation and memory-only saturation batch probes remain unassigned while the real ordinary child is blocked.
Missing, failed, skipped, unfinished, stale or wrong-owner completion of this exact case refuses release qualification.
boundaries: Real child readiness and release; current persisted generation/spec/runtime; separate CPU/memory held footprints; exact claim settlement; subsequent real batch dispatch/terminal result; owned runtime cleanup.

contracts.promise: Owned child exit diagnostics distinguish absent/invalid log reads without inventing readiness.
supported_paths: Real reaped compatibility-mode Bun child; immediate harness exit boundaries preserve their assertion context.
refused_paths: Missing or invalid UTF8 logs cannot silently become empty diagnostics or successful readiness.
boundaries: Diagnostic controls do not establish the unknown startup-stall cause, auth correctness or production deadline changes.

contracts.promise: The same scoped bearer receives matching workload authority across leader apply and follower batch transport.
supported_paths: Existing leader/follower HTTP paths use the same scoped workload decision.
refused_paths: Namespace/role failures cannot silently acquire a broader decision on a second route.
boundaries: Finite command actors and controlled real transport draft; Rust typecheck/discovery/execution are not established here.

contracts.promise: The source-policy guardian recognises the actual shared Deploy permission check while refusing missing or non-enforcing shared checks.
supported_paths: The actual apply handler delegates to the exact shared workload authorizer and propagates its denial; existing direct permission and cluster-admin markers retain their source guard.
refused_paths: Unrecognised helper paths, ignored errors, comment/string-only calls and helpers without a real unconditional Deploy permission call do not satisfy the shared-check guardian.
Optional HostExec or other permission actions do not satisfy the shared Deploy guard.
boundaries: SOURCEPOLICY: these are source parser/AST and route-matrix controls, not runtime request or privilege enforcement proof.
The separate paired HTTP shared-workload authority regression remains required; static guardian success cannot replace it.

contracts.promise: Complete the exact retained legacy OCI case through its finite owned driver.
supported_paths: Exact original ignored test identity and declared Make owner.
refused_paths: No generic aliases or success from another test or owner.
boundaries: Source binding only; real isolated Linux OCI execution and current receipt are required.

contracts.promise: Delegated arrays retain unique accepted outcomes after worker loss.
supported_paths: Multi-node councils and worker ledgers
refused_paths: Duplicate accepted outcomes from a lost worker cannot count twice.
boundaries: The real multi-node gate, including worker loss, must complete on this checkout.

contracts.promise: Real image-backed task arrays enforce shared resources, lifecycle retirement and namespace isolation.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux owned containers with warmed digest-pinned images
refused_paths: Unreserved task capacity and unguarded cross-namespace connections cannot be accepted.
boundaries: These image-backed cases require the warmed-image Linux gate; the network-isolated OCI interruption driver cannot substitute.

contracts.promise: Real image-backed task arrays enforce shared resources, lifecycle retirement and namespace isolation.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux owned containers with warmed digest-pinned images
refused_paths: Unreserved task capacity and unguarded cross-namespace connections cannot be accepted.
boundaries: These image-backed cases require the warmed-image Linux gate; the network-isolated OCI interruption driver cannot substitute.

contracts.promise: A fresh runc task of a named job has its cgroup bound to the job's run identity and its egress allowlist before its command runs.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux owned containers with eBPF and warmed digest-pinned images
refused_paths: A fresh task whose cgroup cannot be bound or held to its allowlist never runs its command.
boundaries: This image-backed case requires the warmed-image Linux gate; the network-isolated OCI interruption driver cannot substitute.

contracts.promise: Cron occurrence IDs survive leader replacement without duplicate dispatch.
supported_paths: Common job lifecycle with durable coordinator and worker state.
refused_paths: No success from admission, stale ownership, or an unaccepted exit.
boundaries: Real execution in the declared gate is required; synthetic evidence cannot qualify the runtime.

contracts.promise: Cron fires use reserved headroom, so one tenant filling every bulk slot cannot lock out another tenant's schedule.
supported_paths: Common job lifecycle on a real three-node council with per-namespace active-run caps.
refused_paths: Bulk arrays past the bulk share are refused with a reason naming the reserved headroom.
boundaries: Real multi-node consensus in the declared gate is required; synthetic evidence cannot qualify the reserve.

contracts.promise: One leader tick commits one Raft entry for every running array, and a worker whose API hangs delays only its own grants.
supported_paths: Task-array dispatch on a real three-node council with many concurrent arrays.
refused_paths: A hung worker's chunks stay with it until the silence timeout, then go to other nodes at the next attempt.
boundaries: Real multi-node consensus in the declared gate is required; synthetic evidence cannot qualify the dispatch cadence.

contracts.promise: Lost singleton owners remain unknown until exact acknowledged replay.
supported_paths: Common job lifecycle with durable coordinator and worker state.
refused_paths: No success from admission, stale ownership, or an unaccepted exit.
boundaries: Real execution in the declared gate is required; synthetic evidence cannot qualify the runtime.

contracts.promise: Singleton API jobs and hooks execute in real containers with encrypted templates and accepted outcomes.
supported_paths: Common job lifecycle with durable coordinator and worker state.
refused_paths: No success from admission, stale ownership, or an unaccepted exit.
boundaries: Real execution in the declared gate is required; synthetic evidence cannot qualify the runtime.

contracts.promise: Crash fixtures retain per-port ownership while their Bun is offline, without keeping network listeners open.
supported_paths: The original fixture can restart on its unchanged gossip/Raft/reporting/API block.
refused_paths: Another fixture process cannot reserve any overlapping block while its lifetime lease remains held.
boundaries: Both TCP and UDP are free at reservation; overlapping per-port file leases survive socket release and release on guard drop.

contracts.promise: Compatible commands reuse one limited container, clean task state and return idle reservations beside application capacity.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux owned runtimes with digest-pinned images
refused_paths: Conflicting or uncertain original ownership cannot authorise reuse or cross-backend replacement.
boundaries: Run through the real Linux gate; protocol mocks do not prove cgroup or namespace isolation.

contracts.promise: One node runs host and image workloads simultaneously and recovers each original backend before a positively retired backend change.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux owned runtimes with digest-pinned images
refused_paths: Conflicting or uncertain original ownership cannot authorise reuse or cross-backend replacement.
boundaries: Run through the real Linux gate; protocol mocks do not prove cgroup or namespace isolation.

contracts.promise: Compatible warm capacity remains available with helper-inclusive reservations, yields to queued owners and refuses revoked queued credentials.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux owned runtimes with digest-pinned images
refused_paths: A retired namespace key cannot authorise a queued command.
boundaries: Real runtime and worker-ledger regression, not throughput or production Raft durability qualification.

contracts.promise: Native helpers reuse durable ownership while fresh host commands enforce CPU, memory and process-tree cleanup.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux native executors on cgroup v2
refused_paths: Uncertain original ownership cannot authorise reuse or release capacity.
boundaries: Real runtime regression; this does not qualify sustained production throughput.

contracts.promise: A job's pids limit becomes its command cgroup's pids.max, the kernel refuses forks past it, and the helper keeps its own limit of 16.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux native executors on cgroup v2
refused_paths: A pids limit of 0 or above 32768 is refused before the job reaches a node.
boundaries: Real runtime regression for the native host executor; shared-runc writes the same task cgroup through the same code.

contracts.promise: A dropped native caller hands its executor to eviction, which retires it and frees its capacity without a restart; a later restart reuses only the originally retired identity.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux native executors on cgroup v2
refused_paths: Uncertain original ownership cannot authorise reuse or release capacity.
boundaries: Real runtime regression; this does not qualify sustained production throughput.

contracts.promise: Native host executors run each command in a limited cgroup, drain and retire it positively, and keep uncertain slots quarantined.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux process nodes with cgroup v2 and the native host executor
refused_paths: Unenforceable host limits, container runtimes on rootful process nodes and reuse of a killed task group are refused.
boundaries: These cases need root and cgroup v2 in the Linux gate; portable runs cannot substitute.

contracts.promise: Cancellation and the attempt deadline interrupt a reusable executor's cold preparation, and the half-started executor is retired with its slot and reservation returned.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux native host executors on cgroup v2
refused_paths: A runtime call is never abandoned halfway; preparation stops only between runtime calls or while waiting for the helper to connect.
boundaries: The helper never connects in these cases; a slow image pull shares the same interruption but isn't exercised by the gate.

contracts.promise: App placement counts the capacity job leases hold, and every job, leased or not, takes the common job lifecycle.
supported_paths: State reports carry task and executor reservations apart from app requests; the leader adds them to each node's allocated total.
A node that cannot fit a placement reports the refusal and the leader moves the replica.
Job test leases live in Raft with a council; their jobs join the lease before admission and cleanup stops and forgets them.
refused_paths: The pre-0.2.0 node-to-node batch routes are gone.
A job in a test lease namespace is refused unless an active job lease owns it.
boundaries: Single scheduling passes, the in-process leader scheduler and a real three-node cluster with a shared executor budget; leadership change through a snapshot reload.

contracts.promise: No two recoveries share an epoch and recovery id; two that land on one epoch both fence as a split, a fenced data directory needs --force and lands above the fencing epoch, a restarted old voter serves nothing before gossip has synced and had its probe window, and a two-node cluster keeps one voter.
supported_paths: In-process clusters on the real cluster runtime and the in-memory Raft router
refused_paths: Recovering a data directory whose fence record says it was fenced is refused without --force.
boundaries: Old voters that can reach only each other, never a node on the newer epoch, still can't learn of the recovery.

contracts.promise: Gossip probes from nodes with the longest names and a full label set fit the 1,400-byte datagram, so those nodes keep acknowledging and stay alive through churn.
supported_paths: In-process clusters on the real cluster runtime over loopback UDP
refused_paths: A directory extension that cannot fit beside the header is left off the datagram rather than sent oversize.
boundaries: A maximally labelled node piggybacks fewer updates per probe; anti-entropy, which carries no extension, makes up the difference.

contracts.promise: An executor start that misses a runtime command's bound retires that executor and runs the command once on a fresh one, within the command's deadline.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux shared-runc executors
refused_paths: A start that fails again is refused after one retry, and an executor that has not positively retired is never replaced.
boundaries: The runtime failure is injected after a real start; a configuration refusal is never retried.

contracts.promise: Cold shared-runc executors for a digest-pinned image this node has already verified and unpacked send no registry request, so a burst of them survives a registry that rate-limits every request.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux shared-runc executors
refused_paths: Local metadata that no longer hashes to its digest is ignored and refetched, and a tag reference always asks the registry.
boundaries: The first pull of an image on a node still reads the registry, and a cold pin fails as before once the registry's retries run out.

contracts.promise: Retired shared-runc executors across namespaces leave no runtime journals, identities or route files behind.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux shared-runc executors
refused_paths: An identity that might still own a live executor keeps its metadata.
boundaries: Real runtime regression; ordinary app instances are not collected.

contracts.promise: relish upgrade start <version> downloads the release build for the platform the nodes report, countersigns it with the operator's external key, and the rolling upgrade completes; a release with other cluster formats is refused before anything is recorded.
supported_paths: Cluster upgrades started from relish against release metadata
refused_paths: A release whose metadata names another protocol or state pair is refused with a fresh-cluster message and no run is recorded.
boundaries: Every node in the harness runs on the test host's platform, so mixed-architecture selection is covered by the relish, orchestrator and plan unit tests.

contracts.promise: A node refuses a volume or config-file host path outside [storage] allowed_host_paths, and always refuses its own storage and security directories, before any runtime state exists.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux runc nodes
refused_paths: An unlisted host path, and another namespace's managed volume under a listed parent, are refused with no bundle or container created.
boundaries: This case needs runc in the Linux gate; the portable supervisor tests cover the same policy with a mock runtime.

contracts.promise: A running shared-runc profile reports CPU and memory from its executor cgroup, labelled by namespace, definition, profile and node, for Mayo and relish top.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux owned runtimes with digest-pinned images on cgroup v2
refused_paths: A task index or run id never becomes a metric label.
boundaries: The executor's cgroup includes its helper, so the sample carries the helper's small overhead.

contracts.promise: An array whose leader is lost while that leader runs its own share finishes with every task accepted once, replaying only the chunks the lost leader held.
supported_paths: Three-node councils with fake runners at a hundred thousand tasks
Three in-process nodes with real shared-runc and cgroup host executors on rootful Linux
refused_paths: A report from the lost leader's still-running executor is never accepted once its chunks are taken back.
boundaries: The in-process leader stops its control plane rather than receiving SIGKILL; the release job qualification (qualify-jobs-sustained.sh) SIGKILLs Bun on real VMs.

contracts.promise: An OCI test's root is unmounted and removed when the test ends, whether it passed or panicked.
supported_paths: Rootful runs that leave workload identity tmpfs mounted beneath the root
refused_paths: A root that can't be removed fails a passing test instead of being left behind.
boundaries: Test-harness cleanup only; production removal of identity mounts is cleanup_identity_dir's job.

contracts.promise: The owned-runc capacity harness keeps its volumes directory until it stops, then unmounts and removes it, whether the test passed or panicked.
supported_paths: Rootful agents that leave workload identity tmpfs mounted beneath the harness's volumes directory
refused_paths: A volumes directory that can't be removed fails a passing test instead of being left behind.
boundaries: Test-harness cleanup only; production removal of identity mounts is cleanup_identity_dir's job.

contracts.promise: A failed rootless OCI test leaves none of its network helpers running.
supported_paths: Rootless runc nodes whose owners supervise slirp4netns helpers
refused_paths: A helper whose command line names only its generation directory is still found through the root's runtime intents.
boundaries: Test-harness cleanup only; production retirement of rootless helpers is covered by the owned_rootless cases.

contracts.promise: A job run no node can run (host commands under mount_isolation, a binary on no node's allowlist) is refused at standalone admission, or failed by the leader with the nodes' reason, instead of staying queued until its deadline.
supported_paths: Standalone nodes and councils on every platform
refused_paths: A run that one eligible node can still take, or that a node refuses only for a passing fault, keeps waiting.
boundaries: Running host tasks under mount isolation is #714; until then host jobs need mount_isolation = false.

contracts.promise: In a cluster the leader refuses a job run no live node can take at submission, with HTTP 422 and the reason the leader's tick would give, from a compact job-capability summary every node advertises over gossip.
supported_paths: Councils on every platform
refused_paths: A run any live node might take, or one a node hasn't advertised its capabilities for, is admitted and left to the nodes and the leader's tick.
boundaries: Gossip says whether a node's allowed_binaries names anything; the paths come from its capability report, and until it has reported, a binary missing from a non-empty allowlist is caught by the tick, as are nodes that leave or change configuration after admission.

contracts.promise: A chaos fault never outlives the Bun that injected it: CPU and memory caps, paused processes and pinned eBPF fault entries are undone when the next Bun adopts its workloads, and CPU and memory faults restore the workload's own cgroup values when they expire.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux with cgroup v2, through the agent's adoption of recorded instances
The owned eBPF loader with maps pinned in bpffs
refused_paths: The pinned egress policy is not cleared along with the fault entries.
boundaries: Dropping an in-process agent stands in for a SIGKILL of Bun; the cgroup and the workload process are real.

contracts.promise: A pushed image survives losing the node it was pushed to: heal counts only live copies and re-replicates from a survivor.
supported_paths: Three-node TLS council with redundancy 2, each node on its own loopback address and the shared registry port.
refused_paths: A dead node's recorded copy never counts towards redundancy, and the image is never reported Lost while a live copy exists.
boundaries: Linux only: the fixture needs 127.0.0.2 and 127.0.0.3. It proves the OCI pull a deploy performs, not an app start under the process runtime.

contracts.promise: docker, podman, skopeo and crane log in to Pickle with an API token, verify the cluster CA, push an image and pull its layers back.
supported_paths: A Pickle TLS listener on a non-loopback address under a name its node certificate carries, with the cluster root CA in /etc/docker/certs.d, /etc/containers/certs.d, skopeo --cert-dir or crane's SSL_CERT_FILE.
refused_paths: A wrong token, a registry certificate from another CA, and a namespace-scoped token pushing outside its namespace are each refused by the client.
boundaries: Linux only, on a host prepared by scripts/standard-clients-host.sh; client versions are whatever the runner image ships and are logged by the gate. oras is not exercised.

contracts.promise: A node restarted from the runc runtime to the mixed runtime routes each running container to the runc owner that launched it, so startup recovery reads it instead of stopping Bun.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux owned runtimes with digest-pinned images
refused_paths: A launch both backends claim stays unrouted, and recovery refuses it as before.
boundaries: Run through the real Linux gate; the portable mixed-runtime tests cover the routing rules with mock backends.

contracts.promise: A cluster spec change reaches one node at a time, a failed rollout is marked RolloutFailed and never retried until the spec changes, and rollback targets survive every node restarting.
supported_paths: Three-node ProcessGrill clusters wired as bun --cluster runs
refused_paths: Re-applying the identical failed spec keeps RolloutFailed; only a different spec clears it.
boundaries: Rollout progress comes from node reports; full leader-coordinated rollouts with a cluster-wide budget are not claimed.

contracts.promise: One app whose ingress route no node can install never stops the cluster catalogue: every node skips that route, logs it, and keeps publishing discovery and ingress for every other app.
supported_paths: In-process clusters on the real cluster runtime, with the invalid spec written straight to the council
refused_paths: relish apply and relish lint refuse an ingress with an unsupported TLS mode, a zero rate or burst, or a rate whose default burst overflows.
boundaries: The skipped route stays uninstalled until its app is reapplied with a valid ingress.

contracts.promise: A volume snapshot whose create was cut between the Btrfs subvolume and its metadata never leaks a hidden subvolume: the next start deletes it, and a metadata-less subvolume without an intent is reported, never silently skipped.
supported_paths: Rootful Linux with Btrfs-backed managed volumes
refused_paths: A metadata-less subvolume with no intent file is reported and kept, because nothing proves it is safe to delete.
boundaries: Run through the real Linux gate on a loop-mounted Btrfs; the portable tests cover every intent decision with plain directories. The power cut itself stays with the Btrfs power-cut fixture of #287.

contracts.promise: A node alive in gossip whose reports stopped keeps its replicas for the stale-node grace, then loses them to the survivors.
supported_paths: Three-node ProcessGrill clusters wired as bun --cluster runs, with one node's agent stopped while its gossip and Raft carry on
refused_paths: The silent node's replica never moves before its reports have been stale for the grace.
boundaries: The grace is measured on the leader's clock from when the node's reports went stale; a node the leader never heard from counts from when it started listening.

contracts.promise: Every [app.*] field is honoured as written or refused with a reason; none is parsed and then silently dropped.
supported_paths: An init container runs its own image (or the app's) with the app's env, decrypted secrets, and volume and config-file mounts.
Inline config files are per instance and keyed on the container path, and go with the instance.
health.port without an app port is probed at deploy and by the rollout gate.
Removing [autoscale] clears its override; narrowing its bounds clamps it.
refused_paths: volumes, config_file, run_as_user and run_as_group on exec or script apps.
A health check with no port, a zero interval, timeout or threshold, or a timeout longer than the interval.
gpu above 0 and egress.allow_franchise.
A volume size the node cannot enforce, or a changed size on an existing volume.
boundaries: Running an init container's own image needs the provisioned Linux root gate; portable cases check the generated spec and the agent's wiring.
Volume size is refused on the node at deploy, not at apply.

contracts.promise: Workload faults reach running job and task-array attempts on whichever node runs them; killed or paused attempts follow the job's own retry and timeout policy.
supported_paths: Attempts in their own runtime instance take every fault
Commands in a reusable executor take kill and pause
refused_paths: Resource and network faults on a command in a reusable executor are refused with a reason naming the executor.
A caller cannot label an app as a job to bypass the replica-minimum rail.
boundaries: Run the cluster and Linux gates; the portable agent tests stand a plain file in for a task cgroup.

contracts.promise: The rollout and GitOps demos run to completion on a real one-node cluster and fail on the first step that does not do what it says.
supported_paths: scripts/demo/rollout.sh and scripts/demo/gitops.sh, each starting its own relish-init cluster on the process runtime.
refused_paths: A demo that exits 0 without printing its completion line, or swallows a failed step, cannot pass.
boundaries: The demos run with this checkout's binaries; they do not exercise a container runtime.
